Cal Sans
nodes.rationale: Brand voice comes from the custom geometric display face at weight 600 with negative letter-spacing; the type split is strict — never body copy in Cal Sans, never a display headline in Inter.

nodes.label: Inter
nodes.rationale: Cal Sans is licensed to Cal.com; Inter at weight 600 with -0.04em letter-spacing is the documented substitution that preserves the weight + tracking signature.

nodes.label: Cal Primary (#111111)
nodes.rationale: Near-black primary is reserved for primary CTAs and h1/h2 display type — Cal.com's button is near-black, not blue; the system is monochrome at the action layer.

nodes.label: Product UI Fragments in Cards
nodes.rationale: Cal.com doesn't paint marketing illustrations of the product; it shows the actual product chrome (calendar widgets, scheduling forms, integration tiles) at small scale embedded in the marketing flow.

nodes.label: Dark Navy Footer
nodes.rationale: The footer is the only dark surface in the system and visually closes every long-scroll page; the light-to-dark transition is part of the editorial rhythm.

nodes.label: Nav Pill Group
nodes.rationale: A small pill-radius wrapper around grouped sub-nav segments; the pill-in-pill treatment is one of Cal.com's signature interactive components.

nodes.label: Copernicus / Tiempos Headline
nodes.rationale: Slab-serif display at weight 400 gives the literary editorial voice; switching to a sans-serif display would make Claude feel like every other AI tool.

nodes.label: StyreneB
nodes.rationale: Humanist sans body — never geometric; Helvetica or Arial would be too neutral and break the warm-editorial feel.

nodes.label: Warm Coral Primary (#cc785c)
nodes.rationale: The cream + coral pairing is the warmest, most editorial interface in the AI-product category — deliberately warm and humanist where most AI brands use cool blue + slate, a counter-positioning against OpenAI and Microsoft.

nodes.label: Cream Canvas (#faf9f5)
nodes.rationale: Warm tinted cream canvas — deliberately not the cool gray-white that every other AI brand uses; the warm tint is the brand differentiator.

nodes.label: Dark Navy Product Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Dark surfaces are where Claude shows its product chrome — code blocks, terminal output, model comparisons; the cream-to-dark contrast is the page's pacing rhythm.

nodes.label: Anthropic Radial-Spike Mark
nodes.rationale: A small black asterisk-like 4-spoke radial glyph that anchors the brand wordmark and doubles as a content marker; never invert the mark to white-on-dark within the wordmark.

nodes.label: Code Window Card
nodes.rationale: The signature visual element of Claude Code product pages — show real code in JetBrains Mono rather than painting marketing illustrations of code.

nodes.label: Cormorant Garamond
nodes.rationale: Documented open-source approximation for Copernicus / Tiempos Headline at weight 500 with -0.02em letter-spacing.

nodes.label: Plain Black
nodes.rationale: Custom rounded display face at weight 500; going to weight 700 reads as bombastic — the rounded character adds warmth that bolder weight would flatten.

nodes.label: Inter
nodes.rationale: Inter at weight 500 with -0.05em letter-spacing is the documented open-source substitute for licensed Plain Black.

nodes.label: 3D Claymation Illustrations
nodes.rationale: Where most data-platform brands play it cool with grids and gradients, Clay leans hard into hand-crafted-looking 3D illustrations (mountains, mascots) as the dominant brand voltage.

nodes.label: Saturated Feature Card Palette
nodes.rationale: Six saturated single-color cards (hot pink, deep teal, lavender, peach, ochre, cream) show product UI fragments at small scale; the colored card IS the primary visual element on every long-scroll page.

nodes.label: Cream Canvas (#fffaf0)
nodes.rationale: Cream-tinted white canvas differentiates Clay from cool-gray competitor sites; the cream-throughout palette is a system contract.

nodes.label: Cream Footer
nodes.rationale: Clay deliberately closes pages with the warm cream footer rather than the standard dark-footer SaaS template — do not add a dark footer.

nodes.label: Electric Yellow Primary (#faff69)
nodes.rationale: Where Snowflake uses cool blue gradients and Databricks red + slate, ClickHouse leans into one electric yellow that does all the brand work; scarcity at the element level + abundance at the band level makes it powerful.

nodes.label: Near-Black Canvas (#0a0a0a)
nodes.rationale: The highest-contrast interface in the database/data-platform category; the system has no light-mode marketing surface.

nodes.label: Inter
nodes.rationale: Single-family approach — Inter at 700/600/400 covers the entire hierarchy without needing a serif or display counter-voice; tightened negative tracking gives the precise engineered feel.

nodes.label: Yellow Stat Callouts
nodes.rationale: Stat numbers in yellow + sans-700 at huge size (779+, 2.8k+, 47k+) carry the credibility moment for a database brand.

nodes.label: Code Window Card
nodes.rationale: Show actual SQL code blocks inside cards — ClickHouse is a database; the code IS the marketing voltage.

nodes.label: CohereText
nodes.rationale: Monumental display headlines with very tight line height and negative tracking; use massive type sparingly.

nodes.label: CohereMono
nodes.rationale: Uppercase mono labels mark category and system markers, especially on product and research pages.

nodes.label: Cohere Near-Black Primary (#17171c)
nodes.rationale: Pill CTAs in near-black or white; the UI shell stays restrained while photography and product mockups carry the color.

nodes.label: Deep Enterprise Green (#003c33)
nodes.rationale: Product hero bands invert into deep green or dark navy; white editorial canvases are interrupted by deep green, dark navy, and image-led CTA bands.

nodes.label: Coral Blog/Taxonomy Chips
nodes.rationale: Coral is used for editorial taxonomy and small warm accents, not as the main CTA system; active chips invert to coral fill with dark text.

nodes.label: Agent Console Card
nodes.rationale: Dark agent-console mockups with status chips and integration badges make AI infrastructure feel controlled rather than speculative.

nodes.label: Trust Logo Strip
nodes.rationale: Intentionally quiet monochrome customer-logos row with very wide vertical spacing — no cards, no borders.

nodes.label: Media-Led Gradient Policy
nodes.rationale: Keep UI surfaces flat; reserve gradient richness for large media panels and CTA image bands — never use saturated gradients as normal UI backgrounds.

nodes.label: Coinbase Blue (#0052ff)
nodes.rationale: The single brand voltage, used scarcely on primary CTAs, the wordmark, and inline emphasis links — an institutional financial brand that happens to trade crypto.

nodes.label: CoinbaseDisplay
nodes.rationale: Licensed display face; Inter at weight 400 with -1.5% letter-spacing is the documented substitute.

nodes.label: CoinbaseMono
nodes.rationale: Every numerical value renders in CoinbaseMono via the number-display token — asset prices and percent changes are tabular.

nodes.label: Display Weight 400
nodes.rationale: Display sits at weight 400, not the 700+ typical of trading platforms, signaling editorial calm and institutional trust rather than fintech-bombastic urgency.

nodes.label: Full-Bleed Dark Hero + Layered Product-UI Cards
nodes.rationale: The dark hero with floating layered dashboard mockup cards is the single most distinctive component; page rhythm rotates white, soft-gray bands, and dark editorial heroes.

nodes.label: Up/Down Price Semantics
nodes.rationale: Trading green/red (semantic-up #05b169, semantic-down #cf202f) is text color only — never used as a button background.

nodes.label: Button Primary (Pill)
nodes.rationale: Every CTA is rounded.pill (100px); pill for interactive, 24px card-radius for containers, full circle for icons — sharp corners absent.

nodes.label: Inter (Substitute)
nodes.rationale: Documented substitute for the licensed CoinbaseDisplay/CoinbaseSans families.

nodes.label: abcDiatype
nodes.rationale: Single sans family carries display, body, nav, and captions — no display/body family split; display sits at weight 500, confident but not bombastic.

nodes.label: Composio Blue (#0007cd)
nodes.rationale: Single deep-electric-blue voltage carries every primary CTA, wordmark, and spotlight glow.

nodes.label: Terminal Mockup Grid (2x2)
nodes.rationale: Four-pane terminal-style mockup (2x2 dark code/output panels) with a central blue spotlight glow is the brand's strongest visual signature, used as the homepage hero anchor.

nodes.label: Spotlight Glow
nodes.rationale: Radial blue gradient centered behind hero content; the atmospheric backdrop that pairs with 2x2 terminal mockups.

nodes.label: Near-Black Canvas (#0f0f0f)
nodes.rationale: Dark monolithic canvas runs top to bottom; depth comes from brightness-step elevation, not drop shadows.

nodes.label: Button Primary
nodes.rationale: Compact 8px developer-tool CTA radius — use rounded.md for every CTA, not full pills.

nodes.label: Inter (Substitute)
nodes.rationale: Open-source substitute for licensed abcDiatype at weight 500 with letter-spacing -1.5%.

nodes.label: CursorGothic
nodes.rationale: Licensed single sans family; display stays at weight 400 with negative letter-spacing for a magazine voice; Inter is the documented substitute.

nodes.label: Cursor Orange (#f54e00)
nodes.rationale: The single brand voltage reserved for primary CTAs and the wordmark — used scarcely.

nodes.label: Warm Cream Canvas (#f7f7f4)
nodes.rationale: Warm-cream editorial canvas instead of the typical dark IDE atmosphere; a quietly-confident developer brand that believes in editorial calm.

nodes.label: AI Timeline Pastel Palette
nodes.rationale: Five pastel pills (peach/mint/blue/lavender/gold) mark AI-action stages — Thinking, Reading, Editing, Grepping, Done — inside in-product timeline visualizations; never used as system action colors.

nodes.label: IDE Mockup Card
nodes.rationale: Multi-pane IDE mockup (sidebar + editor + chat + terminal) is the only elevated element; hairline-only depth, no drop shadows.

nodes.label: JetBrains Mono
nodes.rationale: Code surfaces are roughly half the page — every code surface renders in JetBrains Mono.

nodes.label: Dell 1996 Inspired
nodes.rationale: An inspired interpretation of Dell.com's 1996 design language: a catalog-era enterprise web design built around a literal black page frame, vivid flat color-block ribbon cards tinted in sage, salmon, periwinkle, sky, peach and lime, chunky Helvetica-Black display titles, Times Roman body copy, and an entire vocabulary of pre-Photoshop hand-cut GIF stickers.

nodes.label: Page Frame
nodes.rationale: The literal black border around the entire viewport (~8px). The design treats the browser window as a printed picture frame; collapsing it to 4px on tablet is acceptable, but removing it entirely loses the brand.

nodes.label: Ribbon Cards
nodes.rationale: The brand's signature component: a white title bar with a sharp black underline, a tinted body block in one of eight catalog colors, and a beveled product photograph notched into the right edge. Flat color blocks only - no gradients, no shadows, no opacity.

nodes.label: Dell Red (#e91d2a)
nodes.rationale: The brand's signature red, reserved for only two things: the homepage CTA panel (cta-block-red) and the top-right phone number (phone-callout). Never decorative, never a card body fill.

nodes.label: Frame Ink (#000000)
nodes.rationale: Pure black. The page frame, top banner background, button fills, and all 1px ribbon-card hairlines.

nodes.label: Hand-Cut GIF Stickers
nodes.rationale: A pre-Photoshop overlay vocabulary: the yellow BUY-a-DELL tab, angled NEW! bursts, round red PC Magazine Readers' Choice seals. Depth cues are hard-edge 1px borders or hand-painted bevels baked into the GIF - never soft CSS shadows.

nodes.label: Arial Black
nodes.rationale: System-stack display face (no webfonts in 1996) for the chunky stenciled section eyebrows (DIMENSION DESKTOPS) at weight 900, all-caps, normal tracking.

nodes.label: Times Roman
nodes.rationale: System-stack serif for every paragraph, caption, and inline anchor. Sans for UI, serif for body - the inverse of modern convention and a dead giveaway of mid-90s typography.

nodes.label: Classic Link Blue (#0000ee)
nodes.rationale: Classic Mosaic/Netscape 3.x default link blue for underlined inline anchors (Copyright, Terms of Use) - the unmistakable 1996 link colour.

nodes.label: Ribbon-Card Tint Family
nodes.rationale: Eight catalog colors, one per product line (olive, sage, salmon, peach, lime, sky, steel, periwinkle). Saturated but just below true neutral chroma - the signature of GIF-era web-safe-palette quantization.

nodes.label: CTA Block Red
nodes.rationale: The homepage's vivid Dell-red panel ("At Dell.com, we'll help you find the right system"). One per page maximum - Dell red is reserved for this and the phone callout only.

nodes.label: Phone Callout (1-800-213-DELL)
nodes.rationale: Red on black, pinned to the top-right of every page. In 1996 the website existed to drive phone-call orders - the phone number IS the navigation.

nodes.label: ElevenLabs Design Analysis
nodes.rationale: A voice-AI brand whose marketing surfaces read like a quietly editorial print magazine: off-white canvas (#f5f5f5) holding warm near-black ink (#292524). Brand voltage is photographic, not chromatic - soft pastel atmospheric gradient orbs are the only color moments.

nodes.label: Waldenburg Light
nodes.rationale: The licensed display serif at weight 300 - the editorial signature. Never bold, never heavy; display sizes pull -0.32 to -1.92px tighter.

nodes.label: Inter
nodes.rationale: Body, navigation, captions, and buttons at 400/500 with +0.15 to +0.18px letter-spacing - the slightly looser editorial dialect.

nodes.label: Atmospheric Gradient Orbs
nodes.rationale: Soft radial pastel blooms (mint, peach, lavender, sky, rose) drift through hero bands and feature sections as pure atmosphere - never button fills, text colors, or component backgrounds.

nodes.label: Ink Pill
nodes.rationale: The single primary CTA: near-black ink fill (#292524) at full pill radius. There is no saturated CTA color and no neon accent in the system.

nodes.label: Off-White Canvas (#f5f5f5)
nodes.rationale: The base page floor holding warm near-black ink. Cards float above it via 1px hairlines and a single subtle shadow tier (0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.04)).

nodes.label: Audio Waveform Card
nodes.rationale: A waveform visualization card holding a play button, waveform glyph, and voice metadata - white surface card, xl radius, 24px padding.

nodes.label: Voice Library
nodes.rationale: The product's core browsing surface: transparent voice rows with 1px hairline dividers and 32px circular voice-icon plates (rounded full).

nodes.label: Button Primary (Ink Pill)
nodes.rationale: Near-black ink pill: background primary (#292524), on-primary text, pill radius, 10x20px padding, 40px height.

nodes.label: EB Garamond (Substitute)
nodes.rationale: Documented open-source substitute for Waldenburg at weight 300 - slightly more humanist than Waldenburg; GT Sectra is the closer alternative.

nodes.label: Notion Purple Primary CTA
nodes.rationale: Signature purple pill (#5645d4) is reserved for the dominant CTA only - the recognizable 'Get Notion free' button color that anchors the brand.

nodes.label: Rectangular-Sober Button Geometry
nodes.rationale: Buttons use rounded.md (8px) rectangles, deliberately NOT pills - a documented choice distinguishing Notion's sober editorial geometry from pill-button-everywhere competitors.

nodes.label: Centered Hero Layout
nodes.rationale: Centered hero composition chosen to stand apart from the left-aligned norm of most B2B SaaS landing pages.

nodes.label: Pastel Feature Card Palette
nodes.rationale: Pastel card tints (peach, rose, mint, lavender, sky, yellow) echo the colorful database properties of the live Notion product.

nodes.label: Embedded Workspace UI Mockup
nodes.rationale: A real Notion workspace UI mockup (Ramp HQ kanban board) breaks out of the hero with a deep diffuse drop shadow so visitors see the live product on the page.

nodes.label: Flat Surface Card Treatment
nodes.rationale: Elevation is capped at level 0-1 for cards; tables and documentation cards stay flat with hairline borders and no heavy resting shadows.

nodes.label: NVIDIA Green Accent
nodes.rationale: #76b900 carries every primary CTA, every active tab, every link affordance on dark surfaces, and decorative corner squares - the entire brand signal in one color.

nodes.label: NVIDIA-EMEA Typeface
nodes.rationale: NVIDIA-EMEA is brand-locked to every text role; the closest open-source pairing is Inter (weights 400/700) while Arial is the official documented fallback.

nodes.label: Two-Surface Chapter Architecture
nodes.rationale: Deep black surface-dark hero/footer chapters frame a paper-white canvas body, alternating in a predictable rhythm so air comes from surface contrast, not padding.

nodes.label: Hyper-Angular 2px Geometry
nodes.rationale: rounded.sm (2px) on every element gives the precise, technical feel of CAD engineering output rather than warm consumer software.

nodes.label: Green Corner-Square Motif
nodes.rationale: A 12x12px solid NVIDIA Green square anchored to a card corner is the system's only consistent ornamental device and its identity tag.

nodes.label: Single-Accent Color System
nodes.rationale: Exactly one accent color does all the work and nothing else competes - the system is intentionally one-color and the brand green is treated as precious.

nodes.label: Hairline-Bordered Flat Cards
nodes.rationale: Cards do not lift: card separation comes from 1px hairline borders and surface-soft backgrounds, with drop shadows reserved only for sticky chrome.

nodes.label: PlayStation Blue Primary
nodes.rationale: PlayStation Blue (#0070d1) is the universal primary CTA and footer surface - reserved and precious, at most one full-bleed blue band per page.

nodes.label: PlayStation SST Typeface
nodes.rationale: Proprietary SST sans renders display copy at weight 300 (light) - unusual for a gaming brand - which gives chrome an airy, editorial quality; Roboto Light and Inter are the closest open-source substitutes.

nodes.label: Three-Canvas Chapter System
nodes.rationale: Alternating black, white, and PlayStation Blue full-bleed bands scroll like a console launch trailer; the section background change IS the divider.

nodes.label: Light-Weight 300 Display Headlines
nodes.rationale: Display headlines render at weight 300 (light) so copy reads as information rather than decoration and the imagery does the storytelling.

nodes.label: Fully-Rounded Pill CTAs
nodes.rationale: Every CTA is a fully-rounded pill at rounded.full (9999px); CTAs are always pills - no medium-radius buttons.

nodes.label: Commerce Orange Store CTA
nodes.rationale: Commerce orange (#d53b00) is the only warm color in the system and is reserved exclusively for store/buy/pre-order actions, never marketing chrome.

nodes.label: PlayStation Plus Gold Gradient
nodes.rationale: The only gradient in the system - a three-stop gold (ffce21 to ee8e00) reserved exclusively for the PS Plus tier banner, never used on other components.

nodes.label: Flat Surface Card Treatment
nodes.rationale: No resting shadow on cards; depth is built from surface-color contrast across band chapters and cards lift only on press.

nodes.label: Imagery-Dominant Sections
nodes.rationale: Game key art and console renders occupy 60-90% of every band with copy compressed into a small editorial slot - imagery does the storytelling.
